**Bottom line:** As of October 13, 2026, nothing I found shows Grok 4.8 on xAI's release notes, so the question would resolve **No** today. The real question is whether it ships, or at least gets mentioned in the notes, within the next ~32 days.

**The resolution source (docs.x.ai release notes)**
I couldn't open the page directly. The most recent third-party check I found: as of September 28, 2026 there was no xAI announcement, model page, price or release note for Grok 4.8. On September 20, Grok 4.8 did not yet have a public API model page or technical report. **Check the page yourself**; a pre-release mention such as a deprecation notice or "coming soon" would also count for Yes.

**Status quo**
- Grok 4.7 is the latest model. It shipped September 21 at Grok 4.6's price.
- Earlier release dates: Grok 4.6 on Aug 12, 2026 and Grok 4.5 on Jul 8, 2026. That's gaps of about 35 and 40 days, which would put 4.8 around late October if the pattern holds.

**Recent news, by date**
- **Sept 13 (9:24 PM ET):** Musk said "Grok 4.8, which is a 2.5T model trained with our new C++ software stack, will finish training this week and start RL".
- **Sept 14:** Musk said 4.8 'will be a noticeable improvement' over 4.7, with 4.9 'probably Astra/Fable class'.
- **Around Sept 28:** a developer tool's commit showed a grok-4.8 family in Cursor's server model list. The reported names were grok-4.8-high, -high-fast and -xhigh-fast (single source).
- **Sept 29:** xAI's own public grok-build repo lists grok-4.8 in its model picker and router tests. Leaker Mark Kretschmann said xAI is preparing the release but "It could could still take one or two weeks."
- I found no news from October about a release.

**Things that argue against Yes: Musk's timelines slip**
Before Grok 4.7 came out, Musk gave at least five different release dates, from "within four weeks" on July 24 to "ten days" on September 1, and every one slipped. Grok 4.8 is also a bigger model built on a new software stack, which could add delays. No release date has been announced and nothing is scheduled before Nov 15.

**Prediction markets**
ArtificialWatch shows Polymarket odds for the next Grok (4.8 or later): 10% by Oct 31 and 88% by Nov 30. I saw this on Oct 13, 2026, but the page doesn't show when the numbers were last updated or how much has been traded, and the jump between the two dates looks odd. Check Polymarket directly.

**Other risks to watch**
- Under the resolution rules, the question also fails if xAI skips 4.8, for example by jumping to 4.9 or 5.
- Releases that only go to certain partners at first also matter. Grok 4.7 was reportedly released first for Cursor, so check whether a partner-only launch got a release-notes entry.

criterios: This question resolves as **Yes** if a version of Grok that is specifically numbered 4.8 has any mention for any reason at SpaceXAI's [Release Notes](https://docs.x.ai/developers/release-notes) before November 15, 2026. If this does not occur for any reason, including that X AI changes its numbering scheme (such as skipping 4.8 or changing it to 4.80), this question resolves as **No**.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** About 32 days, through November 14, 2026.  
(b) **Status quo:** No. The available research has not found “Grok 4.8” in the specified release notes.  
(c) **Reference class:** The last two reported Grok 4.x version gaps were 35 and 40 days. Both would fit within the 55-day span from Grok 4.7’s reported launch to this deadline, though two examples make a weak base rate.  
(d) **No scenario:** The larger model or new training stack causes a delay past the deadline, or xAI uses a different version number.  
(e) **Yes scenario:** xAI adds a Grok 4.8 launch—or even a pre-release mention—to its release notes in the next month.  
(f) **Technicality:** It need not launch to resolve Yes; **any mention** of a version specifically numbered 4.8 on that page counts. A mention only of “4.80” would not.

The recent version cadence and reported preparation favor Yes, but the lack of a confirmed release-notes entry and the risk of delays keep this well short of certain.

Probability: 70%

**(a) Time left:** About 32 days, from October 13 to November 15, 2026.

**(b) Status quo:** No. Grok 4.8 has no entry on the release notes yet. The latest third-party check found nothing as of September 28, and I found no October release news.

**(c) Reference class and base rate:**
- **Release cadence:** recent Grok point releases came 35–40 days apart (4.5 on Jul 8, 4.6 on Aug 12, 4.7 on Sep 21). Applied to 4.7, that points to roughly late October to early November. The window is inside that range, but with little margin.
- **Musk's timelines:** his stated dates slip almost every time. Grok 4.7 arrived about two months after his "within four weeks" claim.
- **Base rate:** a model that is publicly in RL, with model IDs already in partner and xAI repos, ships within the next month roughly 50–60% of the time. Some of those releases would not show up in the release notes in time.

**(d) No scenario:** RL on the 2.5T model, built on a new C++ stack, runs long. Musk keeps saying "soon," and the release slips to late November or December. Alternatively, xAI ships first in the consumer app or to Cursor only, with no docs.x.ai entry before November 15. Or xAI renames or skips 4.8.

**(e) Yes scenario:** RL wraps in October, as the leaker's "one or two weeks" and the grok-4.8-high and -xhigh-fast IDs suggest. xAI launches in late October or early November with an API model page and a release-notes entry. Even a "coming soon" or Cursor-partner mention in the notes would count.

**(f) Technicalities:**
- The model must appear specifically as "4.8" on the docs.x.ai release notes page.
- An app-only launch, or an announcement only on X, does not count.
- Any mention on that page counts, even a pre-release one.
- Skipping to 4.9 or 5 resolves No.

**Market read:** The Polymarket ladder (10% by Oct 31, 88% by Nov 30) puts most of its probability on November. Taken at face value, it gives perhaps 40–50% for a release by mid-November. However, the update time and liquidity are unknown, so this is weak evidence. Release-notes lag and partner-first launches push the estimate slightly down. The strong readiness signals (model IDs in repos, training reportedly finished in September) push it up.

Probability: 48%

(a) **Time left until outcome:** 33 days (from October 13, 2026 to November 15, 2026).
(b) **Status quo outcome:** No (Grok 4.8 is not currently mentioned in the release notes).
(c) **Reference class and base rate:** Point-release intervals for xAI models (Grok 4.5 to 4.6 took 35 days; Grok 4.6 to 4.7 took 40 days). Under this cadence, point releases occur within a 55-day window roughly 70–80% of the time, though larger architectural shifts and frontier scaling runs show a wider variance and higher delay rates.
(d) **Scenario resulting in No:** The 2.5T model's reinforcement learning and post-training evaluations face alignment or infrastructure bottlenecks on the new C++ stack; Elon Musk's timelines slip into late November or December; or xAI skips 4.8 directly to Grok 5 / 4.9.
(e) **Scenario resulting in Yes:** Having begun RL in mid-September and already showing up in tool integration commits and xAI test routers by late September, Grok 4.8 finishes evaluation and enters API availability (or a staged developer preview/changelog entry) between late October and early November.
(f) **Technicalities:** The version must be specifically numbered "4.8" (a jump to 4.9, 5, or a renumbering to 4.80 resolves No). Any mention for any reason (even deprecation, coming soon, or beta notice) on `https://docs.x.ai/developers/release-notes` suffices.

Considering the cadence puts a nominal launch around late October to early November, but factoring in frequent Musk timeline slippages, the complexity of a 2.5T model on a new stack, and potential API release documentation lag, the odds favor Yes, but not overwhelmingly.

Probability: 58%
